nodes.name: Presence (spatial/physical)
nodes.definition: The sense of "being there" in a mediated/virtual environment. This cluster's most contested and most treated construct — split between technology-determined (Witmer & Singer) and psychologically-determined (Chow, Lombard & Ditton) readings; see debate axis 3.

nodes.name: Social presence / co-presence
nodes.definition: The sense of others as meaningfully present/salient in a mediated communication or shared environment. The construct row Strand F was added to ground; splits into a CMC-tradition reading (Short/Williams/Christie via Gunawardena, Garrison) and a VR-collaborative reading whose connection to the CMC tradition is largely this cluster's own construction (see §5, debate axis 10).

nodes.name: Immersion (technological)
nodes.definition: The objective, measurable technological capability of a system to deliver sensory fidelity (Slater's sense; contested by Witmer & Singer's more individual-experience-based account).

nodes.name: Agency / interactivity
nodes.definition: The learner's capacity to act on and change the virtual environment; one of Dalgarno & Lee's core affordance categories.

nodes.name: Embodiment / self-representation
nodes.definition: The learner's sense of having a body/avatar within the virtual environment.

nodes.name: Cognitive load (extraneous vs. germane)
nodes.definition: Working-memory demand imposed by the medium/task; extraneous load (irrelevant to learning) is this cluster's primary mechanism for the "more immersion, less learning" finding.

nodes.name: Affect: enjoyment & intrinsic motivation
nodes.definition: Positive emotional/motivational response to the learning medium; the mechanism CAMIL's affective pathway and Makransky & Lilleholt's SEM both route through.

nodes.name: Situational interest
nodes.definition: Momentary, task/content-triggered interest (distinct from stable trait interest).

nodes.name: Self-efficacy
nodes.definition: Learner's belief in their own capability to perform a task; frequently treated as a proximal outcome/mediator in Strand D's professional-education literature.

nodes.name: Engagement / flow
nodes.definition: Sustained attentional/behavioral absorption in the learning activity.

nodes.name: Learning outcomes: retention & transfer
nodes.definition: Declarative/conceptual knowledge gain, measured on post-tests, transfer tasks, or delayed retention. This cluster's single most-treated construct.

nodes.name: Learning outcomes: procedural / skills
nodes.definition: Hands-on, performance-based competency (e.g., medication administration, clinical procedure); Strand D's primary outcome type.

nodes.name: Cybersickness & physical discomfort
nodes.definition: HMD-induced nausea/disorientation/eye strain; a substantive design constraint documented most fully by Cossio et al.

nodes.name: Representational fidelity
nodes.definition: The degree to which the virtual environment visually/perceptually resembles the real referent; one of Dalgarno & Lee's affordance categories.

nodes.name: IVR (HMD)
nodes.definition: Head-mounted-display delivered immersive virtual reality — one pole of the cluster's central media contrast.

nodes.name: Desktop-3D / non-immersive VR
nodes.definition: Screen-mediated 3D virtual environment without a headset — Part III's own primary lab-condition proxy.

nodes.name: 2D video / slideshow / text
nodes.definition: Conventional non-3D instructional medium — Part III's own deployment-condition proxy.

nodes.name: Screen-based virtual patient / sim
nodes.definition: Interactive, screen-mediated simulated-patient scenario used in health-professions education.

nodes.name: Conventional instruction (control)
nodes.definition: Traditional, non-simulation instructional comparison condition.

nodes.name: Home vs classroom setting
nodes.definition: Deployment-context contrast holding medium constant — the direct empirical analog of Part III's own lab/deployment poles.

nodes.name: SEM / process model (no media contrast)
nodes.definition: Structural-equation/path-model design testing mediation within a single medium, without a between-medium comparison.

nodes.name: Review / meta-analytic aggregate
nodes.definition: Systematic review or meta-analysis synthesizing multiple primary studies.

nodes.name: CAMIL (Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning)
nodes.definition: Makransky & Petersen's dual-path (cognitive/affective) theoretical model of learning in immersive VR; this cluster's single most-cited theoretical synthesis node.

nodes.name: Dalgarno & Lee's 3D-VLE Affordances Model
nodes.definition: The learning-affordances framework for 3D virtual learning environments (representational fidelity, learner interaction, task authenticity, collaboration); empirically tested by ped-sec-24.

nodes.name: Lombard & Ditton's six-conceptualization presence taxonomy
nodes.definition: The field's foundational typology of presence definitions (social richness, realism, transportation, immersion, social actor within medium, medium as social actor).

nodes.name: Witmer & Singer Presence Questionnaire (PQ/ITQ)
nodes.definition: The origin instrument for self-report VR presence measurement, with its companion Immersive Tendencies Questionnaire.

nodes.name: Community of Inquiry (CoI) framework
nodes.definition: Garrison, Anderson & Archer's three-presence model (cognitive, social, teaching) for online educational transactions; Strand F's single most-cited internal hub, itself contested by ped-sec-31.

nodes.name: Cognitive presence (CoI component)
nodes.definition: CoI's construct for the process of constructing meaning through sustained reflection/discourse; related but distinct from social presence.

nodes.name: Teaching presence (CoI component)
nodes.definition: CoI's construct for instructional design/facilitation/direction; related but distinct from social presence.

nodes.name: Gunawardena Social Presence Scale (SPRES)
nodes.definition: Gunawardena & Zittle's Likert-scale operationalization of social presence for CMC contexts, with sub-factors including intimacy, immediacy, affective/social association, and co-presence/salience-of-others; an alternative to Short et al.'s original semantic-differential measure, itself later critiqued as incomplete by ped-sec-27/ped-sec-29.

nodes.name: Kreijns/Kirschner/Jochems's CSCL Pitfalls
nodes.definition: Two named pitfalls in computer-supported collaborative learning design — the automatic-interaction assumption and the cognitive-only restriction — that suppress genuine social interaction.

nodes.name: Mayer et al.'s methods-not-media critique
nodes.definition: The explicit argument that 20 years of media-comparison research yielded no reliable IVR learning advantage, while value-added (within-medium) research reliably improves outcomes — this cluster's primary export for debate axis 2.

nodes.name: Short, Williams & Christie's Social Presence Theory (1976)
nodes.definition: The origin theory (external to this cluster — no in-cluster unit is the 1976 source itself) positing that communication media vary in their capacity to transmit the sense of interpersonal presence; the shared ancestor every Strand-F unit engages, contests, or revises.

nodes.name: Cook et al.'s Technology-Enhanced Simulation meta-analytic framework
nodes.definition: The pooled-effect-size framework (knowledge, skills, behaviors, patient effects) anchoring debate axis 6's "simulation beats no-intervention" pole.

nodes.name: media richness / reduced social-context cues
nodes.definition: The communication-theory account that a medium's own bandwidth/cue-richness determines the interpersonal presence it can convey; explicitly rejected by Garrison, Anderson & Archer (ped-sec-26).

nodes.name: community of learning / sense of community
nodes.definition: The felt sense of belonging to a learning group, related to but distinct from social presence proper.

nodes.name: Presence Questionnaire subscales (Control/Sensory/Distraction/Realism)
nodes.definition: Witmer & Singer's own four-factor structure for the PQ, cited by Chow (ped-sec-03) as an exemplar of the technology-determined reading of presence.

nodes.name: Extraneous processing / seductive details
nodes.definition: Task-irrelevant cognitive load induced by immersive/high-fidelity stimuli, competing with germane processing.

nodes.name: Methods-not-media (Clark's distinction)
nodes.definition: Clark's (1983) argument that instructional method, not delivery medium, drives learning outcomes; extended by ped-sec-12 to physical deployment context.

nodes.name: Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ)
nodes.definition: The standard cybersickness self-report instrument, originally designed for flight-simulator contexts; its fitness for HMD-VR is contested by Cossio et al.

nodes.name: Value-added research design
nodes.definition: A study design that manipulates instructional features *within* a medium rather than comparing across media — the design paradigm Mayer et al. and CAMIL both recommend over media-comparison.

nodes.name: Deployment context (home / classroom / lab)
nodes.definition: The physical/institutional setting in which a VR or desktop-3D learning intervention is delivered; the direct empirical analog of Part III's own lab-vs-deployment poles.

nodes.name: Common-method-variance risk
nodes.definition: The methodological caution that same-administration subjective mediator and outcome measures can inflate SEM path estimates; raised by Makransky & Petersen (ped-sec-11) against their own prior study's methodology.

nodes.name: Real people / projecting oneself socially and emotionally
nodes.definition: Garrison, Anderson & Archer's own working definition of social presence within CoI.

nodes.name: Intimacy / immediacy (SPRES sub-factors)
nodes.definition: Two of Gunawardena & Zittle's named sub-factors within the Social Presence Scale, alongside affective/social association and co-presence/salience-of-others.

nodes.name: Automatic-interaction assumption (Pitfall 1)
nodes.definition: Kreijns et al.'s named critique of CSCL designs that assume social interaction will occur simply because the environment permits it.

nodes.name: Cognitive-only restriction (Pitfall 2)
nodes.definition: Kreijns et al.'s named critique of CSCL designs that neglect the affective/social dimension of group work.

nodes.name: Presence as an existential orientation / individual-differences reading
nodes.definition: The psychologically-determined pole of presence — presence as shaped by the perceiver's own traits, prior experience, and willingness to suspend disbelief, not solely by system fidelity.

nodes.name: EEG workload / overload index
nodes.definition: Physiological (EEG) measure of cognitive processing demand, used by Makransky et al. (ped-sec-10) as mechanistic evidence for the cognitive-load route.

nodes.name: Virtual-lab C1–C4 rubric
nodes.definition: Potkonjak et al.'s own categorization rubric for classifying virtual-laboratory systems by technology type and interaction model.

nodes.name: Debate axis 1: more immersion → more learning ↔ immersion adds presence but not learning

nodes.name: Debate axis 2: media-comparison designs informative ↔ methods-not-media/value-added valid
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-02.

nodes.name: Debate axis 3: presence as technology-determined ↔ presence as psychologically/individually determined
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-03. This cluster's most heavily populated debate.

nodes.name: Debate axis 4: affective route ↔ cognitive-load route
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-04.

nodes.name: Debate axis 5: desktop-3D sufficient proxy ↔ IVR unique affordances
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-05.

nodes.name: Debate axis 6: simulation beats no-intervention strongly ↔ sim-vs-sim differences negligible
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-06.

nodes.name: Debate axis 7: cybersickness as substantive moderator ↔ ignorable side-effect
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-07.

nodes.name: Debate axis 8: deployment context matters ↔ context-equivalence
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-08.
nodes.centrality: core (direct match to Part III's own poles)

nodes.name: Debate axis 9: social presence reliably predicts satisfaction/learning ↔ effects inconsistent/assumed-not-demonstrated
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-09.

nodes.name: Debate axis 10: social presence is medium-general ↔ VR social presence is qualitatively different
nodes.definition: See `debate-map.md` DA-10. Directly documents the CMC-to-VR bridge gap (§5).
